title: 3 dead after vehicle plows into pedestrians in Los Angeles
summary: Three people hit by the vehicle were declared dead at the scene, while two pedestrians and the driver of the vehicle, were taken to hospitals, the Los Angeles police and fire departments said.

blocks.text: Three people hit by the vehicle were declared dead at the scene, while two pedestrians and the driver of the vehicle, were taken to hospitals, the Los Angeles police and fire departments said.
No official details were immediately available about the incident
An SUV plowed into a group of pedestrians in the North Hollywood district of Los Angeles on Tuesday, killing ‌at least three and critically injuring three more, authorities said.

No official details were immediately available about the incident, which happened shortly before 6 p.m. PST. A police spokesperson ​said investigators had yet to determine if the ​crash was accidental or deliberate.

"We need to understand exactly what happened and what led to this tragedy," Los ​Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger said in a statement. "I will ⁠be closely following ⁠the investigation and seeking additional ‌information as the facts emerge."
A damaged car lies at the scene of a vehicle crash, involving multiple fatalities, Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, in the North Hollywood section of Los Angeles. (David Swanson/The Associated Press)
Three people hit by the vehicle were declared dead at the scene, while two pedestrians and the driver of the vehicle, were taken to hospitals, the ⁠Los Angeles police and fire departments said.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the SUV drove onto a sidewalk and struck a group of street ‌vendors and pedestrians, adding that first responders were on the scene and that her office was working closely with city departments.
"I’m heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted," she added on X, ​promising updates as more information came in.

Television station KCAL-TV, a CBS News affiliate, ⁠said a car crashed into a food stand near a bus stop ⁠along Lankershim Boulevard a major road through the busy NoHo commercial ⁠and ⁠arts district in the city's ​San Fernando Valley.
A small white partially crumpled SUV appeared to have ​run up on to the ⁠sidewalk under a blue canopy to hit the side of a mass-transit shelter structure, aerial news images from KCAL showed.
